A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original geometric probing, steering validation across models and methods, and human validation of evaluation labels in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds PCA variance analysis, a random-direction control, and Qwen2.5-14B verification in Appendix K.

M1.justification: The CRH decomposition, probing optimization objective, PCA construction, and steering procedures are retained. Revised probing hyperparameters and the new random-direction control concern evaluation rather than a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use AxBench concepts spanning text, code, and mathematics with AlpacaEval prompts. The supplementary studies retain this task coverage; adding Qwen2.5-14B changes model settings rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds a random-axis/normal-plane probe as an evaluated comparator to the optimized PCA probe. The existing DiffMean, PCA, Mean-Centering, and probe-based steering comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-14B at layers 24 and 36 and protocols for PCA diagnostics and a matched random-direction control. It reconciles conflicting probing norm schedules to 0.1–2.0 times the difference-vector norm and revises the appendix learning rate from 0.01 to 0.1, matching the main text. These reported setting corrections do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix K substantially strengthens scrutiny of the central geometric interpretation: it tests whether three PCA directions capture the optimized-vector variance, whether comparable structure appears with random directions, and whether the three observable implications persist in a larger model. These analyses were absent from v1.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly reports standard deviations and minimum/maximum explained variance across 2,451 cylinders covering 99 concepts. Existing confidence intervals and correlation significance procedures are retained. No additional repeated-run counts or seeds are specified; Table 4's loss standard deviation measures landscape variation.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained, with substantive new diagnostic results. Table 3 reports 95.14% mean variance explained by the top three components. Table 4 reports optimized versus random axis-wise loss ranges of 6.05 versus 1.59 and phase-wise ranges of 0.51 versus 0.07. Figure 25 adds Qwen results, including Pearson 0.019, p = 0.297 at layer 24.

T1.justification: Appendix F.1 in v2 corrects Equations 20–21 to use the unit axis a_d instead of the unnormalized difference vector v_d in the orthogonal projection. This repairs a mathematical normalization error. The theorem statements, assumptions, and remaining derivations are retained; expanded proof sketches mostly explain existing reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain extending LRH through overlapping concepts, explaining sample-specific steering through cylindrical geometry, distinguishing predictable magnitude from unpredictable sectors, and providing empirical validation. Rewritten abstract and conclusion passages preserve these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix K adds interpretations that the PCA cylinder faithfully summarizes local geometry, that structured losses reflect meaningful directions rather than the probing pipeline alone, and that CRH extends beyond smaller models. The original mechanism discussion and substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 makes probing hyperparameter documentation consistent and supplies the new analyses' sample totals, matched objective/norm-budget conditions, and Qwen intervention settings. Hardware, existing data-construction instructions, evaluation prompts, and code-access information are retained. Random-direction generation and repetition details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Ning et al. citation supporting helix-like representations and adds the Qwen2.5 technical report. Rewritten related work more explicitly distinguishes explaining steering variability from improving steering performance, while retaining the central positioning relative to LRH. Several other reference changes update the same works' publication metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract, proof sketches, probing narrative, related work, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Related work moves from Appendix B to main-text Section 7, duplicated probing-process descriptions are consolidated, and the appendix structure is renumbered. These constitute broad editorial reorganization beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–4 and the multipanel Figure 25. Figures 1–24 and Tables 1–2 retain their substantive displays, with limited caption edits, repositioning, and surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: Appendix K adds useful checks on dimensional adequacy, random-direction controls, and model scale. Corrected projection normalization and consistent probing settings also improve accuracy and reproducibility. These provide a clear but limited overall gain: the random control remains incompletely specified, and its categorical conclusion that only semantically meaningful directions produce structure exceeds what the reported comparison establishes.
